author: claude

patch.value: A test that measures the host is one defect; a test that stops measuring anything in order to survive the host is a worse one. The wait budget genuinely is host-dependent, so tolerating a short admission is right, but only while the reason for the shortfall is known. Keeping each rejection's diagnostic is what makes the tolerance sound.
The concurrency contract cannot tell lock admission control apart from a real platform failure

The multi-process no-lost-update test counted only successes, collapsing every rejected writer to a boolean. Relaxing its count assertion to tolerate a slower Windows filesystem therefore made it blind: a writer rejected because the native binary genuinely failed on that platform was indistinguishable from a writer whose lock wait budget simply expired, so the test would have passed through a real platform defect while silently exercising fewer writers.

Every rejected writer's own diagnostic is retained rather than collapsed to a boolean; a rejection carrying the lock-conflict message is tolerated as admission control; a rejection carrying any other message fails the test and names the diagnostic; the assertion is proven non-vacuous by injecting a non-lock failure and observing the test fail.

value.author: claude
value.text: Proven by injection: adding a non-lock rejection to the comment mutation made the test fail with 'a writer failed for a reason other than the lock wait budget: [exit exit status: 2: pm-rust: invalid mutation request: INJECTED non-lock defect]'. Removing the injection restored a pass.

value.author: claude
value.text: A lock timeout surfaces as PmRustError::LockConflict whose Display is: pm item {id} is locked by another writer. Matching the id-independent substring recognises admission control without matching any other failure.

value.author: claude
value.text: When a gate is relaxed to stop measuring the runner,the relaxation must keep the reason for the shortfall observable. Otherwise the fix for a flaky gate is a blind gate.

value.note: captures each rejected writer's diagnostic and asserts every rejection is lock admission control

message: Record the blindness the timing relaxation would have introduced

author: claude

patch.value: append_comment returns Result<(),String> carrying each rejected writer's own stderr; the test asserts every rejection contains the lock-conflict diagnostic and fails naming any other reason.
A writer turned away by the lock wait budget is tolerated; a writer that fails for any other reason fails the test with its diagnostic named.

Injecting a non-lock rejection made the test fail with the injected diagnostic; removing it restored a pass. Gates: cargo fmt --check exit 0, clippy -D warnings exit 0, cargo test --all-targets --all-features 138 passed 0 failed, just changelog-check exit 0.

message: Harden the concurrency contract against blind tolerance
